text:
Support Rep - Maya: FYI customer ACME reports model started serving stale product descriptions right after last canary rollout. They say outputs mention discontinued SKUs that were removed days ago.

ACME SRE: yep, reproducer attached — on a few conversation ids we suddenly see older product text for specific prefixes. Started ~2h after your canary. We didn't change input.

Support Rep - Maya: thanks. can you paste a minimal repro? headers, convo id, model name?

ACME SRE: minimal curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer XXXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-compat-1","conversation_id":"acme-ctr-42","input":"Describe widget-7 prefix: features, warranty"}'
```
Response contains old sku paragraph. We toggled model to `rwd-compat-1-v2` and some requests fixed, but then some calls still return bad text. Seems nondeterministic.

Oliver Chen: rough guess — could be KV/prefix cache not invalidated or shared between model variants during the canary. Did the rollout reuse the same cache key namespace?

Eliot Park: checking deploy notes... DeployBot: "Canary deploy rwd-compat-1 -> rwd-compat-1-v2 started 1769960000, 25% traffic at 1769960800, 100% at 1769961600".

DevOncall Bot: Incident link created: #INC-2026-kv-cache-stale (automated).

Infra Eng - Raj: log snippet from prefix-cache service for convo `acme-ctr-42`:
```
[1769962065] GET key=conv:acme-ctr-42:prefix_hash=0x1a2b model_ns=default -> HIT source=redis shard=3
[1769962070] SERVE model=rwd-compat-1-v2 using kv_owner=default
[1769962082] GET key=conv:acme-ctr-42:prefix_hash=0x1a2b model_ns=default -> HIT source=redis shard=3
[1769962082] served_text_source=kv_cache (cached_at=1769900000)
```
Note cached_at is older than the product change. That indicates we didn't evict on model variant update.

Support Rep - Maya: Customer says they expect prefix cache to be invalidated on model updates that affect tokenizer/behavior. Is that guaranteed today?

Eliot Park: current behavior: prefix/KV cache keys omit model version for space optimization; we rely on rollout compat guarantees. If a new model changes tokenization/semantics and we don't update cache namespace, you can get stale or mismatched outputs. Oops.

Product PM - Dana: For ACME this is high-severity (customer sync with legal). Short-term: can we route their traffic to a non-cached model variant or flush cache for their prefix?

Infra Eng - Raj: We can flush per-customer keys. Command to list keys:
```
redis-cli -h prefix-cache-redis-3 KEYS "conv:acme-ctr-42:*" | xargs -L1 redis-cli -h prefix-cache-redis-3 DEL
```
But that's heavy; better to expire by prefix version tag. We have an admin API:
```
POST /admin/cache/flush
{ "prefix_root": "conv:acme-ctr-42", "reason":"post-deploy stale outputs" }
```
I'll run it if support/PM ok.

ACME SRE: flushing is fine. We need a guaranteed mitigation while you fix the root cause.

Support Rep - Maya: Raj please go ahead. Also please confirm we don't break other customers.

Infra Eng - Raj: Running admin flush for `conv:acme-ctr-42` now...
DevOncall Bot: "Admin cache flush started by Raj for conv:acme-ctr-42"
DevOncall Bot: "Admin cache flush completed, 12 keys removed"

ACME SRE: re-ran the same curl, response now shows updated product text. Thanks.

Oliver Chen: short-term remediation options:
- Flush affected customer prefixes (what we did)
- Route customer to no-cache pathway (set header `X-Cache-Mode: bypass`)
- Roll back deployment to previous model if widespread

Eliot Park: long-term fix proposals:
1) include model version (or model build hash) in cache namespace key (e.g., `conv:{id}:mv:{model_hash}:prefix`) to avoid cross-model contamination.
2) on rollout, if model variant isn't forward/backwards compatible, perform targeted cache invalidation during deployment (deploy hook).
3) add modeled tokenization fingerprint stored in cache entries; on load compare and invalidate if mismatch.

Product PM - Dana: Prefer (1) + (2). Need an RFC and a deploy-safe rollout plan. Also update docs for customers about cache semantics.

Support Rep - Maya: follow-ups for customer: explain what happened, actions we took (flush), and ETA for permanent fix. I'll draft message.

ACME SRE: appreciate fast turnaround. Please let us know when permanent fix is live — this impacted our UI.

Eliot Park: I filed GH issue #redwood/kv-cache-322: "prefix cache should be namespaced by model_build_hash + deployment invalidation hook" with proposed design and migration steps.

Infra Eng - Raj: note for on-prem/private customers: some run local redis instances — we'll provide a migration tool to rekey existing entries during upgrade.

Support Rep - Maya: status: ACME confirmed fix after flush. Next actions:
- Eliot to own RFC + GH issue (ETA 3 working days)
- Raj to add admin flush runbook + safety checks (ETA today)
- Dana to include cache semantics in public doc (ETA 1 week)
- Oliver to coordinate release gating for canary (add cache-ns check)

Product PM - Dana: marking this High. I'll update account team.

DevOncall Bot: "INC-2026 status -> mitigated (customer flushed). Follow up items created."

Support Rep - Maya: thanks team. I'll close with ACME once RFC timeline confirmed. :thumbsup:
